Don't use flowery language and place the reader in first person/ Scenes might include solitary birthdays that morph into insights on self-reliance, quiet dinners that offer space for deep parental bonds, and the mature realization of the weight of carrying family expectations alone. This subject is worth exploring to uncover how the only child experience shapes an individual's outlook on solitude, independence, and family dynamics. response: As I sit alone on my birthday, surrounded by the familiar comforts of my childhood home, I'm struck by the realization that I've spent my entire life carrying the weight of family expectations on my shoulders. (In many ways, this is a hallmark of the only child experience, where the absence of siblings means that the burden of responsibility falls squarely on the individual.) Growing up, I often found myself [bracing] for the pressure to excel academically, socially, and professionally, as if my parents' hopes and dreams were inextricably linked to my own success. (This can lead to a sense of self-reliance, as I've had to navigate the complexities of life on my own, without the support of siblings to share the load.) But as I've grown older, I've come to understand that this self-reliance has also meant carrying the weight of family dynamics alone, (often to the point where I've felt like I'm shouldering the entire burden of our family's happiness). Quiet dinners with my parents have become a rare occurrence, as we've learned to navigate our differences and find space for ourselves. (In these moments, I've come to appreciate the value of solitude, and the importance of prioritizing my own needs and desires.) As I look back on my life, I realize that being an only child has taught me to be resourceful, adaptable, and resilient, but it's also forced me to confront the weight of carrying family expectations alone. (This is a lesson that I'll carry with me for the rest of my life, and one that I hope to pass on to my own children, should I ever have them.)
